what_happened: At the status update that ran at 07:42 UTC on 10 Nov (11:42pm Pacific), the agent took it for the 7:42am Pacific run. It moved Monday's summary into the page archive a run too early and wrote a morning step-back section. No data was wrong. Only the timing of the archive move was off. No job work was judged.
cause: The agent acts on state without resolving what it refers to, and Athena does not guard it. Here the state was which scheduled run was firing. The run-specific steps, such as the archive move at 15:42 UTC, are tied to a run only by the agent's own reading of a clock time in mixed UTC and Pacific. Nothing states the run's identity in one fixed zone, and nothing checks the step against it. Safe use depends on the agent converting time zones correctly.
prevention: A check in the status-update step would have prevented it. It would read the run's trigger time in UTC and compare it to a fixed schedule table that lists each run's steps. It would allow the archive move and the morning step-back section only when the trigger is the 15:42 UTC run, and otherwise refuse and say which run it is. The agent would no longer decide which run it is from a clock reading in two zones.
proposed_request: Make the status-update step identify which scheduled run it is from the trigger time in UTC, using a fixed schedule table in the repo. The table lists each run's UTC time and its run-specific steps. Outcome: the archive move of the previous summary into the page archive and the morning step-back section happen only in the run that fires at 15:42 UTC. In any other run, including the 07:42 UTC run, that step is refused with a message naming the current run and the run it belongs to. Acceptance: a test runs the step at 07:42 UTC and at 15:42 UTC. At 07:42 UTC it makes no archive move and writes no step-back section. At 15:42 UTC it does both. The schedule table is the only place run times are written. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
